subject: Advertising
text: Case Study An Indian sportswear brand, Puma India, had partnered with cricketer Virat Kohli as its brand ambassador to strengthen its market position among young consumers. Kohli’s popularity and strong personal brand image aligned with Puma’s positioning of energy, style, and performance. His endorsement not only created trust but also gave the brand a competitive edge in India’s growing sportswear market. In addition to celebrity endorsement, Puma India actively uses social media platforms like Instagram, YouTube, and Twitter to connect with its target audience. Campaigns such as #DoYou and #LetThereBeSport are shared widely online encouraging participation and influencer tie-ups. By doing this, Puma can directly interact with customers and measure how well the campaign is performing. This combination of brand ambassadors and digital engagement reflects how Indian brands today leverage both traditional trust-building methods and modern, interactive media to reach wider audiences. text: new health drink brand, entered the Indian market promising to energize busy young professionals. Before launch, the team conducted research to understand why people usually picked up energy drinks. They found that most buyers looked for quick refreshment and an image of vitality. Based on this insight, the company developed a strong communication message that connected with the lifestyle of working youth. The central theme revolved around the idea of “staying ahead in the race.” The visuals showed a young professional confidently balancing long hours at work and sports with friends after office. The brand’s message was showcased across television, social media reels, and outdoor billboards. The storytelling relied on an engaging mix of humour and aspiration, capturing attention while also making the brand memorable. The campaign was launched simultaneously in metro cities with a consistent tone and design across all media. Before rolling out, the creative agency prepared a structured note aligning the product promise, target audience, and brand personality.
